summary.title: DevOps — Grokipedia
summary.one_liner: DevOps is a set of cultural, process, and tooling practices that join software development and IT operations to ship changes faster and more reliably, covering its history, principles, and lifecycle.
takeaways: DevOps combines people, processes, and technology to shorten the software lifecycle and release frequently.
The term was coined by Patrick Debois, who organized the first DevOpsDays in Ghent in 2009.
Key terms include pipeline, shift left, everything as code, and AIOps.
Cultural elements such as shared responsibility, blameless postmortems, and psychological safety are central to DevOps.
Lean and Agile principles, along with CI/CD, GitOps, and DevSecOps, shaped the practice from the 2010s into the 2020s.
summary.summary: This Grokipedia entry defines DevOps as a mix of practices, tools, and cultural philosophies that automate and integrate development and operations. It traces the field's history from early 2000s influences such as the Agile Manifesto, through the 2009 DevOpsDays launch and 2010s popularization, to 2020s developments like GitOps, DevSecOps, and AIOps. It then covers cultural foundations (Westrum culture, blameless postmortems), Lean and Agile integration, and the DevOps lifecycle with CI/CD. The page is encyclopedic in style and cites sources throughout, though parts of the text are cut off before the CI/CD section ends.
